claims.text: Post-solidification annealing of HfZrTiTa0.53 can induce a fine-scale ductile intergranular phase.
The induced intergranular phase will improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
The proposed treatment will not substantially compromise yield strength or compressive strength.
The proposed treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
As-solidified HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-solidified HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-solidified HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% uniform tensile strain and limited tensile ductility.
Annealing at 800–900°C for an optimized duration will promote local atomic diffusion.
The promoted diffusion will form a continuous nanometer-scale ductile phase along grain boundaries.
A ductile grain-boundary phase will redistribute stress and delay crack nucleation during tensile loading.
Annealing will facilitate phase separation at grain boundaries and produce a thin ductile film.
The grain-boundary film will accommodate strain more uniformly and moderate tensile stress concentrations.
The matrix will retain its intrinsic high strength after annealing.
Annealing will increase uniform tensile strain by at least approximately 50% relative to the stated 13.5% baseline.
Annealed specimens will retain yield and compressive strengths within approximately 5–10% of their original values.
Annealed specimens will preserve energetic impact performance.
The intervention is applicable only to HfZrTiTa0.53 produced by similar rapid-solidification methods and tested within the stated temperature and strain-rate regimes.

contradictions.description: The same 13.5% value is described as uniform tensile strain in the initial-state and prediction fields but as terminal tensile strain in the baseline. Uniform elongation and terminal strain are distinct measures and cannot be treated as interchangeable without justification.
